original_value: In this paper, we propose a new fingerprint sensing technology based on electrostatic imaging, which can greatly improve fingerprint sensing distance. This can solve the problem of the existing capacitive fingerprint identification device being easy to damage due to limited detection distance and a protective coating that is too thin. The fingerprint recognition sensor can also be placed under a glass screen to meet the needs of the full screen design of the mobile phone. In this paper, the electric field distribution around the fingerprint is analyzed. The electrostatic imaging sensor design is carried out based on the electrostatic detection principle and MEMS (micro-electro-mechanical system) technology. The MEMS electrostatic imaging array, analog, and digital signal processing circuit structure are designed. Simulation and testing are carried out as well. According to the simulation and prototype test device test results, it is confirmed that our proposed electrostatic imaging-based fingerprint sensing technology can increase fingerprint recognition distance by 46% compared to the existing capacitive fingerprint sensing technology. A distance of more than 439 μm is reached.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents a new fingerprint sensing technology based on electrostatic imaging, capable of greatly extending fingerprint sensing distance. It addresses the weakness of existing capacitive fingerprint identification devices, which are easily damaged because the detection distance is limited and the protective coating is too thin. The fingerprint recognition sensor can also be installed beneath a glass screen to satisfy full-screen mobile phone design requirements. The electric field distribution around the fingerprint is analyzed in the paper. Based on the electrostatic detection principle and MEMS (micro-electro-mechanical system) technology, the electrostatic imaging sensor is designed. The MEMS electrostatic imaging array, along with the analog and digital signal processing circuit structure, is developed. Simulation and testing are also performed. Simulation and prototype test results confirm that the proposed electrostatic imaging-based fingerprint sensing technology increases fingerprint recognition distance by 46% compared with existing capacitive fingerprint sensing technology, achieving a distance of more than 439 μm.
